clue.text: Ran up trouble for Dr Fox, first into the doorway with such language as would suit 10 and co.

definitions.text: such language as would suit 10 and co.

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Dr Liam Fox, a doctor who became a Conservative MP

indicators.note: into means the one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a doorway is an entry
A is first, as in A1 or the top grade

explanation.surface: Some unrest over Dr Fox, with talk at the door suited to a band of plotters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges RAN UP and 'into' puts A within ENTRY. Fawkes and his fellows wanted to blow up Parliament, so their talk would hardly be parliamentary; 'first' is A as in A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Unparliamentary language is speech not allowed in the Commons, fitting for men plotting against Parliament itself.

clue.text: Mark of disease — English one: having one I come to Down district pool

annotationWithheld.why: Mark of disease — English one: having one I come to Down district pool (6,9): POCK + E + BILL + I + ARDS are clear, but no reading of the clue gives the T of POCKET without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Mark of disease — English one: having one I come to Down district pool

clue.text: Sounding like champagne, demand your head in concrete terms

indicators.note: says the word for champagne is heard, not read, for the opening sound

parts.note: champagne is fizzy wine
to call for something is to demand it; a call is a demand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An order delivered with a bubbly voice, putting the request in solid terms.
explanation.walkthrough: FIZZY said aloud gives the opening of the answer; 'head' takes Y from 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: Physically means in bodily or material terms, the concrete rather than the abstract.

clue.text: The first cause for 10 and co.

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word The is used

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: The original cause that drove Fawkes and his companions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: treason is the crime charged against Fawkes and his fellow plotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting to kill the king and blow up Parliament was high treason, the charge laid on the conspirators.

clue.text: Explorer's game with no score in 12 with no time

indicators.note: in means the nil score is put inside the trimmed word
with no means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer at 12-across, PLOT
a score of nothing is O, nil

explanation.surface: An explorer's pastime that ends goalless inside a short plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Polo was the Venetian explorer, so the game shares his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a game on horseback, and also the surname of the explorer Marco Polo.

clue.text: XIV split American style, memorable for turning up 16, 4 and 12 …

parts.note: XIV split into XI and V is 11 and 5, the 5th of November as Americans write it

explanation.surface: A Roman fourteen divided the American way, a date remembered for exposing wrongs, treason and a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Remember, remember the fifth of November, gunpowder, treason and plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth of November 1605 is when the Gunpowder Plot was uncovered, still remembered with bonfires.

clue.text: … has its day with monastic office held by designer Mary about New Year

indicators.note: held by means the office sits inside the designer's name

parts.note: Mary Quant, the British fashion designer of the miniskirt era
terce is a monastic office said at the third hour

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: The date has its moment while a monastic prayer is wrapped in a fashion designer's name around New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges N and YEAR into ENARY. The clue continues 6-down: in 2005 the fifth of November marked four hundred years.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatercentenary is a four-hundredth anniversary, the day the 1605 plot's date came round for the 400th time.

clue.text: Awkwardly situated home for relation without right

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: without means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a brother is a relation

explanation.surface: A home made awkward for a relative who has lost his rights.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in bother is an idiom for being in trouble or an awkward position.

clue.text: Nasty note backed by notes of liability

indicators.note: backed means the note's name is turned back to front

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale
IOUs are notes promising to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A nasty message supported by a stack of debt notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repellent, a stronger synonym for nasty.

clue.text: Divisions reported by one of the 21

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard, as if spoken aloud

parts.note: forks are divisions, points where something splits

explanation.surface: Splits in the party passed on by one of the fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is GUYS: Guy Fawkes was one such Guy, whose effigies are still burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes was one of the Guys, a Guy being both his first name and his burnt effigy.

clue.text: Perpetrator of 4 was consumer after a job

indicators.note: after means the eating comes behind the a and the job

parts.note: a post is a job
a consumer eats, so was consumer means ate

explanation.surface: Someone who betrays a cause was eating after getting a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or loyalty, a kind of treason against one's own side.

clue.text: 10 and co.'s ground

definitions.meaning: Fawkes and his fellows had the Gunpowder ...

explanation.definitionFit: Plot means both a conspiracy, the plotters' scheme, and a patch of land.

clue.text: Angled by racket that's angered royal circle

parts.note: cross means angry, so angered
a court is the circle around a monarch

explanation.surface: A noisy disturbance that annoyed the royal entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise but means a tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-court shot in tennis is hit diagonally across the court, angled off the racket.

clue.text: Follower of Dada has not finished a carriage and a table

indicators.note: the last letter of the carriage word is dropped

parts.note: a surrey is a light four-wheeled horse carriage
a list is a table

explanation.surface: An art fan leaves a coach unfinished alongside a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrealism grew out of Dada, so a surrealist is a follower of that movement.

clue.text: Painter on the fiddle didn't finish food

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

indicators.note: the final letter of the instrument is dropped

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: An artist cheating on his dinner without getting through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' looks like cheating but just puts RA before the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is an Italian food of small pasta parcels.

clue.text: Women without their Institute ignored, beaten and abused

indicators.note: beaten means knocked about, so the letters are scrambled
the I for Institute is taken out

parts.note: I for Institute, as in the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: Women's Institute members snubbed, battered and mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' scrambles what is left once 'without their' drops the Institute's I; the women's W leads. Women's Institute is a British countrywomen's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wronged means treated unjustly, as one who has been abused.

clue.text: 12 leader's setback give taxi man new heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the taxi driver is replaced

parts.note: a cabby drives a taxi
set read back to front

explanation.surface: The plot leader's reverse hands the cab driver a fresh core.
explanation.walkthrough: SET reversed is TES; it replaces the central B of CABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Catesby led the Gunpowder Plot conspirators.

clue.text: Left in Yorkshire town, fruit may be past it

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed within the town

parts.note: Selby is a market town in North Yorkshire
a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: Abandoned in a northern town, some fruit has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic phrase 'may be past it': goods can pass this date.
explanation.definitionFit: Food may be past its sell-by date, the last day a shop should sell it.

clue.text: Not a 1 thing to do to have partly kept books

indicators.note: kept means the books are held within
only part of the word have is used, its contracted form

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Something orderly to do, keeping some books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have partly' gives VE, as in the contraction 've.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting is proper parliamentary business, not unparliamentary behaviour.

clue.text: Fatally hold odd number inside

indicators.note: inside means the number sits within the odd word

parts.note: strange means odd
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A deadly grip with a peculiar figure inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is to grip the throat until death.

clue.text: Hospital fellows' alleged appearance

indicators.note: alleged signals a word said aloud

parts.note: guise is outward appearance

explanation.surface: A hospital's men supposedly looking the part.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy's is a London hospital, and guys are men or fellows.

clue.text: Subaltern retaining final word on complaint

indicators.note: retaining means the word is held inside

parts.note: LT, lieutenant, is a subaltern officer
amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A junior officer keeps the last word in a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a mournful complaint or expression of grief.

clue.text: Yesterday's man — who's he? — in battle

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the battle word

parts.note: a fray is a battle
ID, identity, answers the question who is he

explanation.surface: A has-been asked who he is in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A Saturday prize puzzle, so yesterday was that day; Man Friday is Crusoe's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before Saturday, and Man Friday, Robinson Crusoe's companion.

clue.text: Performance with willow by first of batsmen, Grace — pilgrims' leader — 's shot

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of batsmen

parts.note: Robert Aske led the Pilgrimage of Grace rising of 1536
a try is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A cricket feat by a batsman, W G Grace, then a leader of pilgrims having a go.
explanation.walkthrough: W G Grace is a decoy; with willow suggests a cricket bat but means basket weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketry is the craft of weaving willow or wicker into baskets.
